build_order: pre-check: duplicates by name; live old values == spec old values; snapshot life_cycle_stage and life_cycle_stage_status of every record to update (business rule "Update life cycle from legacy" derives them on ANY update while they are empty); live row of each DELETES entry == spec
insert business_app, new_cis; read back sys_id and number; check alm_asset by ci

apply updates one record at a time (Oracle 11i after the inserts: db_server takes the new dbaix950ldn sys_id); re-read; log every changed field plus life_cycle_stage and life_cycle_stage_status; any non-200 response or an "error" key in the body is a failed update ("Validate lifecycle combination" can abort it)
delete the 4 DELETES rows (ledger keeps each full row)

loop check: re-run the generator's loop check against live cmdb_rel_ci (minus the deleted rows), then insert relationships in id order; any non-201 response is a failure. The PDI does not reject loops: "Prevent Recursion in CI Relationships" only blocks child == parent

not_carrying: Contains::Contained by (service group or service grouping)
outage_carrying_types.rule: a child's failure reaches its parent over carrying types; the per-row relationships[].outage_carrying flag is the source

meta.em_alert_format: list of records in the download shape {field: {value, display_value}}, including "synthetic": {"value": "true", "display_value": "true"}. Time fields: value is UTC, display_value is the PDI user's time zone (Europe/London, UTC+1 on 2026-09-14), as the Table API returns them; join alerts to incidents on value only.

em_alert_fields.initial_remote_time: UI label "Initial event generation time" ("Time that the initial event occurred in the remote system"); no field initial_event_generation_time exists
em_alert_fields.group_source: UI column "Group": automated, rules-based, manual, CMDB, secondary or none. Numeric choice codes not verified (no em_alert on the PDI), so value carries the label
sources: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/Tm19yM2Ui3~uN9XFBacppg/bhN9tpP8s~hCtbJBdqBk3g (Monitor incoming alerts, Yokohama: labels Initial event generation time, Group, Parent, Source, Node, Metric Name)
https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/guxhDnVk8OUAJKLm7WZsYA/gCDVSVoWXal2NZ6z9~4SNQ (Event field format: source, event_class, node, type, resource, metric_name, message_key)

https://github.com/tedorigawa001/ServiceNow-MCP/blob/main/src/tools/event-management.ts (em_alert column names incl. initial_remote_time, last_remote_time, group_source, is_group_alert, parent, incident)

meta.em_alert_correlation: The group is made by 'MOCK topology rule: storage CI -> dependent CIs (CMDB relationships, 15 min window)', named in the primary's additional_info.correlation_rule. The shipped Dynatrace rule would group only alerts sharing a problem_id and make dbaix900nyc (isRootCause true) the primary; isRootCause is Dynatrace's own verdict, not ServiceNow's grouping.
deviations: Service group All cannot be renamed: business rule Check group name uniqueness aborts any change to the group named All (Changes on the group All are not allowed). A new service group Trading Services is created instead (parent_group set to All by that rule); R03 and R04 point to it. New CIs 3, CIs after build 2788.
